items.title: Commands
items.text:
• mkdocs new [dir-name] - Create a new project.
  • mkdocs serve - Start the live-reloading docs server.
  • mkdocs build - Build the documentation site.
  • mkdocs -h - Print help message and exit.

items.title: View downloads of Working Papers
items.text:
Downloads aren't only the way to view Working Papers

This metric is only tracking the links that people click to download the Working Papers. If someone views the Working Paper's PDF embed on the page without clicking the download link, that won't be counted in this metric. If you want to track how many people are viewing the Working Papers pages, visit How to see page views.

items.title: Visit CERG's Google Analytics page
items.text:
Ensure you are logged in to your SFU Google account and have gotten access by IT Services. If you don't have access, request analytics access here.

Go to Google Analytics Engagement page

If you aren't already on the "Engagement" page, click the "Engagement" tab in the left sidebar.

Google Analytics Engagement page

Link Clicks vs Actions

On the Engagement page, you'll see two charts: Link Clicks and Actions. We will focus on Link Clicks chart, as that gives us a more reliable view of engagement.

items.title: Choose a date range
items.text:
Click the date range in the top right corner of the page to select a date range for which you want to see page views. You can select a custom date range or choose from the preset options.

Google Analytics date range selection

Tracking Views Over Time

When tracking page views over time, it's important to keep the same date range consistent for accurate comparisons. I'd recommend tracking by month as it is simple to visualize and provides a good balance between capturing enough data and avoiding short-term fluctuations.

items.title: Find metrics for a specific working paper
items.text:
If you want to know how many people clicked the download link for a specific Working Paper, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the Working Paper link in the chart. If it was recently published and has lots of traction, it should be on the first page. Otherwise, you can use the arrows at the bottom of the chart to navigate through the pages until you find the link.

The link name should look like this: Read Working Paper #21

Google Analytics Working Paper link highlighted

items.title: Find metrics for a specific button
items.text:
If you want to know how many people clicked a specific button on the CERG website, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the button text manually in the chart.

The link text should match the button text on the CERG website. For example, if you want to see how many people clicked the "Learn more about Andy" button, look for that text in the chart.

Google Analytics number of button clicks

items.title: Find metrics for a specific URL
items.text:
If you want to know how many people and where they came from to get to a specific page or URL on the CERG website, you can find that information in the Link Clicks chart.

Since there is no search bar, you'll need to find the button text manually in the chart:

  1. Right click on the chart and select "Drill Down".
  2. Find the URL that you want to track. This will give you a general sense of clicked on a button to get to that URL.
  3. Left click on it to make it bold, then right click on it and select "Drill Down". This will show which pages people came from to get to that URL.
  4. To reset, click the reset icon in the top left corner of the chart.
Your browser does not support the video tag.

Example of finding metrics for a working paper URL

Link Source: {not set}

When drilling down to find metrics for a specific URL, you may see some links with the source listed as {not set}. This means that the link was clicked from an external source, such as a social media post or an email.

If you want to track a specific source of traffic, visit Analyze page views.

Google Analytics Pageviews & Sessions page

Click the date range in the top right corner of the page to select a date range for which you want to see page views. You can select a custom date range or choose from the preset options.

Google Analytics date range selection

Tracking Views Over Time

When tracking page views over time, it's important to keep the same date range consistent for accurate comparisons. I'd recommend tracking by month as it is simple to visualize and provides a good balance between capturing enough data and avoiding short-term fluctuations.

items.title: Find metrics for a specific page
items.text:
Use the search bar at the top of the page to search for a specific page by its URL.

  1. Copy the page URL from the CERG website
  2. Paste the URL into the search bar in Google Analytics and press enter.
  3. The search results will show you the page views and sessions for that specific page.

Google Analytics page view results

items.title: Find metrics from a specific source
items.text:
If you want to know how many people visited a page using a link from a specific source, you can use the search bar to filter the results by source.

Enter in the search bar: ?utm_source=example where example is the source you want to track.

For example, if you want to see how many people visited a page from ChatGPT, you would enter: ?utm_source=chatgpt

Google Analytics page view results

Tracking Sources

Go to How to set up link tracking for a list of sources.

items.title: How to set up link tracking
items.text:
This guide will walk you through the process of setting up link tracking for external content CERG produces.

Link tracking is important for understanding how many people are clicking on links to CERG content from external sources, such as social media posts or emails. By setting up link tracking, you can gain insights into the effectiveness of your outreach efforts and make data-driven decisions to improve engagement.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Sources
items.text: Each link you want to track should have a source associated with it. The source you use will be dependent on what platform or channel the link is being shared from.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: List of sources you can use
items.text:
• email - for links shared in emails (e.g. CERG newsletter)
  • linkedin - for links shared on LinkedIn
  • sfu - for links shared to SFU (e.g. SFU News, SFU social media posts)
  • facebook - for links shared on Facebook

etc.

Using a consistent source name is important for accurate tracking.
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Attach the source to the link
items.text:
To attach the source to a link, append ?utm_source=example to the end of the link, where example is the source you want to track.

So sharing a link to a CERG event on LinkedIn would look like this:

https://www.sfu.ca/politics/CERG/events/fall-2026-wp-21-alternatives-to-fossil-fuels.html?utm_source=linkedin
path: How to set up link tracking

items.title: Track the link in Google Analytics
items.text: Once you have set up link tracking, you can track the link in Google Analytics by following the steps in Analyze page views.
path: How to set up link tracking
